wb6_movement.topic: The barrier, the checkpoints and the roads

claims.text: The barrier's constructed and projected length is 713 km, more than twice the Green Line; about 65% complete; 85% of its route runs inside the West Bank; completed it will isolate 9% of the West Bank including East Jerusalem; about 11,000 Palestinians in the Seam Zone need permits to live in their homes; about 150 communities have land there; farmers use 69 gates, mostly open only in the olive harvest; permit rejection rose from 31% in 2014 to 67% in 2020 and 42% in 2021.

The ICJ advisory opinion of 9 July 2004, by 14 votes to 1 (Buergenthal dissenting), found the wall's construction in the occupied territory contrary to international law, that it must be dismantled and reparation made, that settlements 'have been established in breach of international law', and that the Fourth Geneva Convention applies de jure; the General Assembly endorsed it 150–6–10; Buergenthal agreed settlement-protecting segments violate IHL but found the self-defence analysis dubious; Israel said the wall's sole purpose was to combat terrorist attacks from the West Bank and that it was temporary.

As of December 2025 OCHA documented 925 movement obstacles restricting 3.4 million Palestinians: 89 permanently staffed checkpoints, 218 partial checkpoints, 232 road gates (159 frequently closed; over 120 installed in 2025), 114 linear closures, 167 earthmounds and 105 roadblocks; 43% more than the 20-year average of 647; at least 459 hinder access to main roads, 121 on Road 60; over 14,000 Palestinians between the barrier and the Green Line must coordinate access; 36% of 87,427 patient permit applications were denied or pending.

Israel expanded Route 443 in the 1980s by expropriating thousands of dunams, the court accepting it was meant to serve Palestinian needs; from 2002 Palestinians were banned from it; in December 2009 the High Court ordered the total ban lifted; the army's new arrangements still exclude Palestinians from using it as the main route to Ramallah; more than 100 shops along it closed.
